key_insight: A large-scale, game-sourced dataset captured with a novel dual-screen stitched method provides realistic, temporally-coherent RGB plus multi-channel G-buffer data at scale, narrowing the domain gap for generative inverse and forward rendering.
problem_solved: Existing synthetic datasets lack realism and temporal coherence needed for scalable generative rendering research; this work supplies a high-fidelity, continuous dataset to address that bottleneck.
method: Curate dynamic, visually-complex scenes from AAA games to obtain realistic visual variability and effects.
Capture synchronized RGB plus five G-buffer channels using a novel dual-screen stitched capture pipeline to produce continuous frames.
Assemble and release 4M continuous frames at 720p / 30 FPS across diverse scenes and environments to enable training and evaluation.
impact: Provides ML practitioners with a large, realistic, temporally-consistent dataset that improves training and evaluation of generative inverse/forward rendering models, speeding progress toward real-world applicability.
